key_insight: Introduce *-PLUIE: a personalisable, task-specific extension of ParaPLUIE that uses perplexity-based yes/no prompting (no text generation) to produce confidence scores that better align with human judgments while reducing compute and post-processing.
problem_solved: Automated LLM-as-a-judge evaluation is accurate but costly and requires text generation plus post-processing; there is also limited task-specific personalization for alignment with human preferences.
method: Build on ParaPLUIE: use model perplexity over targeted Yes/No prompts to estimate confidence without generating full answers.
Create *-PLUIE: task-specific prompting variants and user-personalisable templates/thresholds to better match task definitions and rater preferences.
Evaluate alignment by comparing *-PLUIE confidence scores to human judgments and measure practical gains in compute and post-processing overhead.
impact: Provides a cheaper, faster, and customizable way to evaluate generated text that preserves alignment with human judgment—making large-scale NLG evaluation more practical for researchers and engineers.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: input example → task-specific Yes/No prompt → perplexity scorer → confidence score
Bar/line chart: human agreement (correlation) for *-PLUIE vs. standard LLM-judge and baseline automatic metrics
Icon/infographic highlighting compute & post-processing reduction (e.g., clock + CPU → down arrow)
Prompt templates + calibration slider visual showing personalization of thresholds or wording
paper_title: *-PLUIE: Personalisable metric with Llm Used for Improved Evaluation
paper_authors: Quentin Lemesle, Léane Jourdan, Daisy Munson, Pierre Alain, Jonathan Chevelu
